definitions.explanation: the phase of the moon when it is not visible from Earth because it is positioned between Earth and the sun

examples.english: On new moon nights, you can see the stars well.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{新月|しんげつ}な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{見|み}えない→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: Since today is a new moon, you can't see the moon.

examples.japanese: {新月|しんげつ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{満月|まんげつ}→満月：17598_mangetsu⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧2⟦{週間|しゅうかん}→週間：00988_shuukan⟧⟦かかる→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧。
examples.english: It takes about two weeks from new moon to full moon.

notes:
MOON PHASES:
- {新月|しんげつ} (new moon) - moon not visible
- ⟦{三日月|みかづき}→三日月：17597_mikazuki⟧ (crescent moon)
- ⟦{上弦|じょうげん}→上弦：08869_jougen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧ (first quarter moon)
- ⟦{満月|まんげつ}→満月：17598_mangetsu⟧ (full moon)
- ⟦{下弦|かげん}→下弦：23013_kagen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧ (last quarter moon)

FORMS:
{新|しん} (new) + {月|げつ} (moon) → new moon

ASTRONOMY NOTE:
During a {新月|しんげつ}, the moon is between Earth and the sun, so the illuminated side faces away from Earth. This is also the time when solar eclipses can occur.
